title: Train a tiny network
hook: A network of 105 numbers learns a spiral in your browser: forward, backward, a gradient check, and the same block inside every SD 1.5 transformer.

verified.claim: Every transformer block in the SD 1.5 U-Net has a FeedForward: Linear, then GEGLU, then Linear, four times wider in the middle, gated by default.
The browser lab's forward pass, loss and backward pass match PyTorch's autograd to 1e-12 on the same weights, for ReLU, tanh, sigmoid and linear.
The browser lab's gradient check agrees with its backward pass to under 1e-5 relative, and catches a backward pass with the tanh derivative left out.
All tables come from this lesson's lab, run here on a CPU.
Centred differences, the relative error and its thresholds are as in the CS231n notes.

unchecked: The √(2/n) starting scale for ReLU is the rule usually credited to He et al. 2015; we read the abstract, which does not state the formula.
Training results come from one seed and one dataset each; another seed can take more or fewer steps.
How fast the browser lab trains depends on the device; we only ran it on one desktop.
